Cc: Mira Chan <mira.chan@heliosconsulting.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Team operating framework + QBR talking points (leadership review)

Team —

Attaching a first-pass comms + slide notes for next week’s QBR and the proposed operating framework (see attachment org_comm_plan_v1.docx and QBR_slide_deck_v3.pptx). Big picture: tighten ownership across product/infra/platform pillars and reduce cross-handoff drag for model onboarding.

What I need from you by EOD Monday: 1) one-sentence redlines for any phrasing you think escalates risk (security/comms/legal); 2) a single-line alternative for slide 3 (role wording) if you want softer language; 3) any names to exclude from public comms.

Key bullets in the draft:
- Why: reduce time-to-production for models by clarifying product vs infra responsibilities
- What: consolidate model readiness owners into two squads (Model Delivery + Model Platform)
- When: phased rollout during May; public comms w/c May 4, follow-up 2-week check-in
- Ask: leadership preview on May 1 (30m)

I kept the tone direct but not prescriptive — expect iteration. Mira is copied; she validated the timeline with People Ops and will advise on wording for the All-Hands.

Thanks,
Priyom
Head of Platform Programs
Redwood Inference

Priyom —

Thanks for the draft. Quick inline notes after a skim:
- Slide 2 (metrics): add a token-level latency SLA and a % of API calls using cached prefixes — those make the impact more tangible for execs.
- Language around "consolidate owners" is fine for leadership but I’d prefer "clarify and align owners" for external-facing comms — avoids sounding like a removal.
- Can we add one short FAQ bullet on what this means for Dedicated customers?

I flagged a couple of suggestions directly in the deck. Happy to hop on a 20m tomorrow to walk through.

Jonas
VP, Product

Good starter. A few tone suggestions:
- Replace "consolidate" with "simplify and align" where the audience is broader.
- For the folks impacted by role changes, we should include a line: "no involuntary changes without prior 1:1 and People Ops alignment" — that will reduce rumor risk.
- Consider adding a short "what stays the same" slide referencing SLAs and existing support channels.

Also +1 to Jonas on the Dedicated customer FAQ. Happy to draft that short blurb if helpful.
